- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80.0 after peak), model should adjust downward with increasing amplitude.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — increase downward forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0% buffer below observed low.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misread trend — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast curve.
- When true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 3 days, adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction — e.g., if sentiment is bullish but price drops, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast slope.
